facts.statement: Chiayusuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph belonging to the family Stomatosuchidae.
facts.quote: Chiayusuchus is an extinct genus of stomatosuchid crocodylomorph.

facts.statement: Fossils of Chiayusuchus have been discovered in the Xinminbao Group in Gansu, China.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Xinminbao Group in Gansu, China.

facts.statement: Chiayusuchus lived during the Barremian and Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It existed during the Barremian and Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Although initially classified within Stomatosuchidae, Chiayusuchus is now distinguished by having a different teeth shape.
facts.quote: Although it was once considered as member of Stomatosuchidae, it is denied by having different teeth shape.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Chiayusuchus is Stomatosuchidae.
Chiayusuchus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Chiayusuchus is Chiayusuchus cingulatus.
The time range recorded for Chiayusuchus in the Paleobiology Database spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
